questions.question: State Snell's law of refraction. If the refractive index of glass is 1.5, find the speed of light in glass.
questions.solution:
**Snell's law:** n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r — the ratio sin i/sin r is constant for a pair of media.

n = c/v → v = c/n = (3 × 10⁸)/1.5 = **2 × 10⁸ m/s**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Light bends toward the normal entering a denser medium — the single sentence behind every refraction diagram.

questions.question: What is total internal reflection? State two conditions for it to occur.
questions.solution:
**Total internal reflection** is the complete return of light into the denser medium when it meets a rarer boundary beyond the critical angle.

(1) Light must travel from **denser to rarer** medium. (2) Angle of incidence must **exceed the critical angle** (sin C = 1/n).
questions.knowledgeNote: Fibre optics, sparkling diamonds, and mirages are all TIR applications — name one for the extra mark.

questions.question: A fish is 1.2 m below the water surface (μ = 4/3). At what apparent depth does it appear to an observer above the surface?
questions.solution:
Apparent depth = real depth / μ = 1.2/(4/3) = 1.2 × 3/4 = **0.9 m**.

The fish appears raised — which is why spear-fishing aims below the seen position.
questions.knowledgeNote: Apparent depth = real/μ (viewed from rarer); apparent height = real × μ (viewed from denser) — keep the direction straight.

questions.question: Find the critical angle for a glass–air boundary if the refractive index of glass is 1.5.
questions.solution:
sin C = 1/n = 1/1.5 = 0.6667 → C = **41.8°**.

Any ray inside glass striking the boundary above 41.8° is totally reflected.
questions.knowledgeNote: Denser medium → smaller critical angle: diamond (n = 2.42) has C ≈ 24°, hence its fire.

questions.question: On what factors does the lateral shift of a ray through a glass slab depend?
questions.solution:
Lateral shift x = t·sin(i − r)/cos r increases with: (1) **thickness** of the slab, (2) **angle of incidence**, and (3) **refractive index** of the glass.

The emergent ray stays parallel to the incident ray — only displaced sideways.
questions.knowledgeNote: Zero thickness or normal incidence → zero shift; the parallel-emergent-ray result is the exam diagram.

questions.question: What are totally reflecting prisms? Write two of their uses.
questions.solution:
Right-angled isosceles glass prisms that turn light by 90° or 180° through **total internal reflection** instead of silvered mirrors — no absorption losses.

**Uses:** (1) periscopes (two such prisms); (2) binoculars (folding a long path into a short body); (3) SLR camera viewfinders.
questions.knowledgeNote: TIR prisms beat mirrors on efficiency — that is why quality optics uses glass, not silver.
